title: Ronnie Knows Best: Legal Aid You Didn't Ask For
description: Legal trouble night on Snazzie FM. Ronnie opens the mailbag for listeners drowning in court dates, denied claims, and contractor disputes, and answers every single one with the same useless cure: just don't sign it. Barry reads the actual law into a void.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're on Snazzie FM, and tonight, folks, we crack open the mailbag for Legal Trouble Night. You wrote in, you're scared, you've got court dates. And I have answers.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, I want it on the record that neither of us is a lawyer.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Lawyers are just people who read the document, Barry. And reading, frankly, is what gets folks into this mess. First letter. Carol from the marina writes, quote, I got a jury duty summons for a six week trial, it overlaps my only paid vacation, and it says I'll be fined or held in contempt if I ignore it. I don't know how to ask for a deferral. End quote.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: There's a deferral form, Carol. Most courts let you request a new date online, it takes five minutes.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: No, no, Barry, you're overthinking it. This is junk mail. The court can't just subscribe you to a trial without your opt in consent. Carol, here's what you do. Write UNSUBSCRIBE on the envelope and mail it right back.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That is not... a summons is not a newsletter, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And above all, Carol, and write this down, do not sign it. You don't sign, you're not in it. Next. Marcus, who emailed us at midnight, says, quote, my landlord is keeping my whole security deposit for vague damages, I have photos showing the place was spotless, and the small claims deadlines are confusing me. End quote.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Keep those photos, Marcus. That's your evidence. File before the deadline and bring the pictures.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: See, that's where Marcus loses. I won a deposit dispute once on pure vibes and eye contact. Paperwork only weakens you, Marcus, it gives them something to read.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Gives them... the photos are HIS, Ronnie, they help him.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Delete the photos, Marcus. No evidence either way, totally neutral, very fair. And whatever the landlord hands you, you do not sign it.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: He's deleting his only proof. I need everyone to know I said don't.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Heartwarming. Now, Priya, longtime listener, writes, quote, my disability claim was denied over a typo in my date of birth, the appeal window is thirty days, and the phone line disconnects me every time after two hours on hold. End quote. <p:0.3> Priya, I feel this in my bones. The automated lady and I have history.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: The fix is the typo, Priya. You file the appeal in writing within the thirty days and attach your birth certificate. Don't rely on the phone.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Or, Priya, simpler. From now on, just have a different, correct date of birth. Start telling everyone you're a Capricorn, establish a paper trail. And un-sign the original claim, so the typo retroactively never existed.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That is not how birthdays work, Ronnie. That is not how anything works.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Birthdays are a suggestion, Barry. Okay, Big Dale couldn't get through, so Barry, you read this one.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Fine. Big Dale writes, quote, a contractor took my deposit, never finished the deck, stopped answering my calls, and now there's a mechanic's lien on my house for work that was never even done. End quote.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Well first off, congratulations, Dale. A lien on the property? That's lakefront. You're sitting on waterfront real estate now, my friend.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: A lien, Ronnie. L I E N. It's a legal claim on his house. There is no lake.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Ohhh, the sticker kind. Yeah, a lien is just a sticker the bank slaps on your house, Dale, you peel it right off. Then finish that deck yourself and bill the contractor for the privilege of learning from you.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: You cannot peel off a lien. You dispute it. In court.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And the lien, Dale, do not sign the lien. <p:0.3> And if it's already signed? You sand it down.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Sand it d... it's a filing, Ronnie, it's not a coffee table.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Last one, and it's a big one. Anonymous writes in, although they did sign it, so, hi, Kevin. Quote, I'm facing an actual misdemeanor charge, court date next Tuesday, I've never once reached my public defender, should I just show up. End quote.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Yes. Yes, Kevin, you show up. You show up early. Not showing up is its own crime.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Kevin, you represent yourself. But here's the genius part. As a different person. The charges are filed against you. They can't find a you that isn't there.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, that's impersonation, that's a second charge.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And when the judge starts talking, you ask to see the judge's license. Establish who's really in charge. Then, and this is the move, Kevin, you un-sign the verdict before they even read it.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: You can't un-sign a verdict, Ronnie, you don't sign verdicts at all.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Exactly. So it's already un-signed. <p:0.3> Legally, if you never sign the guilty, you stay innocent. That's just math, Barry.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That is not math. That is the opposite of math.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And speaking of results, a follow up just came in. Carol from the marina, our very first letter, she took the advice and mailed back her summons marked UNSUBSCRIBE.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: She's in contempt of court now, Ronnie. There's a warrant out for her.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: See? It worked. She never has to do jury duty again. <p:0.3> Don't sign the warrant, Carol.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: She can't. <p:0.3> They're bringing it to her. That's Snazzie FM, where we are still, for the record, not lawyers.
